podcast.body: This song became a number one hit on the pop chart in 1971 and a top 10 R&B hit. It served as the theme song for their 1972 Saturday morning cartoon. Songwriter George Jackson, an R&B artist from FAME Studios, Muscle Shoals, Alabama, specifically wrote it with The Jackson Five in mind, but The Osmonds recorded it there instead. "And one bad apple not only went to number one on the pop chart in 1971 It was a top 10 R&B hit too."

podcast.body: Topping the Hot 100 in early 1971, this song was originally a Jackson 5 reject turned down by Motown's Berry Gordy. The Osmond Brothers remade it into an "uncanny Jackson 5 facsimile," and it notably prevented The Jackson 5's own "Mama's Pearl" from reaching number one. "the Osmonds One Bad Apple was literally a Jackson 5 Reject. A song Motown's Barry Gordy turned down for his superstar family band that was then remade by the Osmond Brothers into an uncanny Jackson 5 facsimile."
